boundary_note: Bounded first pass for the frozen Jenkins' Ferry record (April 30, 1864) in the Camden Expedition [April 1864]. The April 29 rear-guard skirmishing near the Saline bottom and the retreat to Little Rock (May 3) are context. Campaign-wide marches, returns, foraging and multi-action loss totals are context; they are not assigned to one record or added across records. Draft claims do not alter model inputs.

claims.rationale: No inspected return establishes matched personnel at a common opening boundary. The frozen side-specific numerical strength bounds are blank (missing_numeric_strength). No figure in this pass is adopted as a simultaneous opening force.

claims.value: The frozen force field reads Department of Arkansas [US] and Army of Arkansas [CS]; the live field reads zero. Britton says Steele had not more than 4000 men on the field and that Kirby Smith, with ten brigades, must have had nearly 10,000 at an estimated 1,000 per brigade; he says the three infantry divisions from Louisiana numbered about eight thousand on arrival near Camden. Price says Churchill's division fought greatly outnumbered.
claims.rationale: Retrospective estimates, one derived from an assumed brigade strength, and an interested statement; no return. None is adopted as a matched opening strength. The live zero is not measured absence.

claims.value: Price says Kirby Smith assumed command of the Army of Arkansas in person on April 26 and conducted its later operations, Price commanding the Arkansas and Missouri infantry divisions. Britton says Kirby Smith sent Dockery north of Toxie Creek and still had Walker's division to commit, that Rice posted the Union line, and that Steele sent Salomon three regiments. The frozen commanders are General E. Kirby Smith and Major General Frederick Steele; the live page gives Edmund Smith as Lieutenant General.
claims.rationale: Command roles from an interested report and a history; the listed commanders do not receive automatic sole credit, and no rank is adopted.

claims.value: The frozen result reads Union victory in retreat and the live result Union Victory. Price says the enemy yielded the ground, leaving dead, wounded, wagons and pontoons; Britton says Steele repulsed every assault and then withdrew across the river unmolested; NPS says the Federals repulsed the attacks and crossed.
claims.rationale: Retain the original result and engagement interval; later movements and campaign contribution are different measures. No new probabilities or individual causal credit. NPS's statement that the Confederates bungled a chance to destroy Steele's army is a counterfactual judgment.

claims.value: The frozen casualty text reads 964 total (US 521; CS 443); the live field reads 1700 (US 700; CS 1000). Britton gives the Union loss as 86 killed, 500 wounded and 61 missing; cites Cunningham for a Confederate loss of about 800 killed and wounded; gives incomplete returns for Price's three divisions of 99 killed and 437 wounded; and guesses Walker's loss was nearly as large. Price says two guns of Ruffner's battery were lost.
claims.rationale: Original casualty returns were not inspected; preserve totals, categories, cutoffs and differences. No canonical reconciliation or casualty-based opening count; related actions must not be added without resolving population overlap.

open_questions: Steele's reports (No. 2), Salomon's, Rice's, Garrett's and Crawford's reports (Nos. 5-6, 21, 34), Kirby Smith's report (No. 93), Cunningham's narrative (No. 94), Churchill's, Tappan's, Parsons's, Clark's, Waul's and the other Confederate reports (Nos. 58-70) and the incomplete returns remain deferred.

NPS/CWSAC is one family. Wiley Britton's The Civil War on the Border, volume II (Putnam's, 1899) is a retrospective history described on its title page as based upon official reports and the author's observations; it gives figures from Union and Confederate reports and incomplete Confederate returns, so it is not independent of the Official Records families. Price's report dated Camden, May 1864 is one family of interested Confederate accounts. Official Records Series I, Volume XXXIV, Part 1 is a shared container, not an additional witness. Report dates are not event times or proof of contemporary knowledge.
No automatic commander attribution, causal campaign score, morale/readiness number or battle/campaign double counting.
